subject: Post-call: MedixHealth hosting options and isolation asks
messages:
From: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>
To: Alice Moreno <alice@medixhealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 15 Aug 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call: MedixHealth hosting options and isolation asks

Hi Alice — thanks again for taking the time this morning. Quick recap and the asks we captured so we can move toward a POC.

Call highlights (short):
- Primary constraint: MedixHealth will be processing PHI and requires no risk of cross-tenant data exposure; network and execution isolation are hard requirements.
- Target SLOs you mentioned: 99.95% availability; latency targets around p95 < 300ms for single-turn gen (512-token avg); sustained throughput ~600 reqs/min with occasional spikes to 1.2k.
- Data residency: US-East for all stored artifacts; KMS for key management and audit logs retained for 13 months.
- Decision factors: isolation guarantees (noisy neighbor mitigation), SLA credits, evidence for SOC2 controls and operational runbooks.

Questions / requests for you:
1) Is co-tenancy at the serving layer strictly disallowed, or would a logically isolated tenant on dedicated pool (single-tenant GPU pool per customer) be acceptable as an intermediate option prior to full VPC?
2) Does procurement need a redline-able SLA (we have a standard 99.95% with credits, we can put a tailored addendum in the contract)?
3) Any specific compliance team contact for the security questionnaire (we can loop them into the next call).

Suggested next steps (our recommendation):
- Week 1: Dedicated-capacity POC (reserved GPU pool per workload tenant) to validate latency and noisy-neighbor isolation.
- Week 2: If required, a short private-VPC evaluation (bring-your-own-VPC) to validate network isolation and KMS integration.

I attached a short tenancy scoring matrix and a draft SLA for your legal/procurement review. Ben will follow up with technical isolation details (KV cache isolation, container boundary and GPU pool guarantees).

If that approach sounds reasonable, can we book a 45-min technical deep-dive early next week with your infra/security folks?

Thanks,
Jonas Weber
Enterprise Account Executive
Redwood Inference

Attachments: SLA-draft-MedixHealth.pdf, tenancy-scoring-matrix.csv

From: Alice Moreno <alice@medixhealth.com>

Subject: Re: Post-call: MedixHealth hosting options and isolation asks

Jonas — thanks for the clear recap. A few clarifications from our side: 

- Co-tenancy: For any environment that processes PHI we cannot accept shared tenant kernel or shared model-weight residency. We may consider a dedicated GPU pool per customer (single-tenant GPU allocation) but we need documented isolation guarantees (network + compute + cache).
- SLO detail: 99.95% is baseline; procurement will push for a commercial SLA statement with explicit credits. Provide the exact SLA wording and historical uptime for the last 12 months if possible.
- Noisy neighbor: provide concrete mitigation strategies and metrics you monitor (e.g., per-tenant GPU utilization thresholds, preemptive autoscale headroom, eviction behavior, KV-cache flush policies).
- Security: send your SOC 2 type II report + the answers to our questionnaire (we attached the questionnaire in a separate email to security@medixhealth.com). We also need KMS integration details and proof of key separation per-tenant.

If dedicated capacity plus documented isolation meets our controls, we can avoid the operational overhead of a private VPC. However if any of the isolation pieces are missing we will require a private VPC + HSM/KMS that we control.

Please include Ben/DevOps in the next message with technical specifics and timelines.

Best,
Alice Moreno
Head of Partnerships & Integrations
MedixHealth

Attachments referenced: MedixHealth-security-questionnaire.xlsx (sent separately)

Subject: Re: Post-call: MedixHealth hosting options and isolation asks

Alice — looping Ben (Solutions) and Grace (Product Ops) to answer the technical/compliance asks below. High level answers up front, details below.

High level: dedicated capacity (single-tenant GPU pools) plus our standard KMS integration satisfies the majority of PHI requirements for customers we currently serve. We can also run a private VPC/on-prem eval if your security team prefers full customer-managed networking and HSM controls.

Concrete isolation controls we provide (summary):
- Compute isolation: Dedicated GPU pools per customer (no shared model weight residency when dedicated selected). Pools are scheduled onto isolated job queues; tenanted jobs are pinned to the reserved pool.
- KV cache and memory: Per-tenant KV cache namespaces; caches are zeroed on job completion and not shared across namespaces.
- Network isolation: For Dedicated we use tenant-specific subnets and strict egress rules; for Private we hand off VPC peering and customer-managed subnets.
- Preemption + noisy neighbor mitigation: we maintain per-tenant resource quotas, pre-warmed autoscale headroom (configurable), and can apply soft QoS priorities for internal background workloads. For extreme contention we have automated fallback to a lighter quantized model variant with throttled throughput rather than degrading tail latency for other tenants.
- Audit & evidence: SOC2 Type II and operations runbooks (we include audit logs, key usage logs, and per-route tracing). We will share the SOC2 report under an NDA if needed and include a runbook excerpt in the POC pack.

SLO / SLA specifics (proposed):
- Availability: 99.95% monthly uptime; SLA credit tiers in draft SLA (attached).
- Latency targets (observed in our fleet under similar configs): p50 ~ 70ms, p95 ~ 280ms for single-turn 512-token workloads on our recommended model family on Dedicated. We will publish p50/p95 for your test workload during the POC.
- Observability: token-level cost/latency breakdowns + per-route dashboards during POC.

POC proposal:
1) Dedicated POC (2 weeks): reserved GPU pool, run your representative traffic driver, we provide perf report + isolation test checklist.
2) Optional Private VPC evaluation (3 days) if you need network/HSM proofing after results from Dedicated.

Next steps we propose:
- Confirm whether procurement needs redlined SLA now or after POC.
- Schedule 45-min tech deep-dive (Ben + Grace + your infra/security). William from our infra team can join to walk through tenancy safeguards.

I attached the tenancy scoring matrix and a draft SLA for convenience. Ben — can you add a short ops checklist and a proposed canary rollout plan in the thread?

Thanks,
Jonas Weber
Enterprise Account Executive
Redwood Inference

Alice / team — short ops checklist and canary plan below. Happy to walk through this on the call Jonas will schedule.

Ops checklist (for Dedicated POC):
- Provision reserved GPU pool (spec: 4x A100-equivalent nodes) and pin Medix workload queue.
- Enable per-tenant KV namespaces and zero-on-complete policy.
- Configure KMS integration; verify key separation and audit logs.
- Setup per-route dashboards and synthetic traffic runner (we will provide the runner).
- Run isolation test suite: cache bleeding tests, eviction/residency tests, and burst soak at 2x normal traffic.

Canary rollout suggestion (post-POC):
1) Internal pilot on 10% of traffic (timebox 72 hours) with active monitoring on p95 latency, error rates, GPU thermal metrics.
2) Increase to 50% if metrics stable for 48 hours.
3) Full cutover with SLA addendum signed.

We will attach the ops playbook and the tenancy scoring matrix in the shared folder. Proposed timeslot for the technical deep-dive: Wed 23 Aug, 10:00-10:45 PT — does that work?

Regards,
Ben Carter
Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
